scope: The opt-in tools panel replaces Views ScrollView with a Rust-owned viewport controller and a native clipping/event/window adapter. The platform scrollbar/input/accessibility adapter remains native; Views retains the original ScrollView behavior through a shared interface.

contracts: Tools forms now use PanelViewport. The opt-in host is a custom View with a Rust ScrollViewportState and clipping adapter, not Views ScrollView. Rust owns viewport/content/bar allocation, overlay versus reserved width, content extent, authoritative offset, maximum, resize/rebuild clamps and minimum-movement reveal policy. Native Views mode retains ScrollView through the same interface.

The adapter supplies preferred control/font sizes, native scrollbar thickness/overlay facts and platform input requests. The existing platform scrollbar retains appearance, wheel/trackpad/momentum/key/AX delivery; Rust admits and applies each resulting position. Content translation and clipping are native window/compositor adapters; existing Metal control canvases receive viewport refresh callbacks. Remaining platform scrollbar/event and per-control View identities are not claimed migrated.

The Rust model preserves finite fractional requests, rejects nonfinite offsets, clips reveal targets to content/viewport and disables movement for zero-sized viewports. Model state is not copied from a native ScrollView offset in the opt-in path. ScrollView synchronization/subscription ownership was removed from the tools shell; weak refresh callbacks are owned by the Rust viewport view. Views keeps its original paint path without an extra Metal refresh observer.

Browser-service stores, profile/workspace/generation and captured-key admission, confirmation, history/query timers, Rust form/catalogue/geometry/input state and persistence remain unchanged. Other scroll surfaces, including preferences, remain native and are future work.

Five Rust regressions cover overlay/reserved geometry, resize/rebuild clamping, native minimum-movement and oversized-target reveal behavior, fractional/nonfinite requests and empty/tiny/extreme metrics. A shared browser oracle compares a real Chromium ScrollView at four sizes using 20 position requests and 60 reveal requests, including wrapped content and transition to no overflow. The effective range comes from live content/viewport extents; a visible native scrollbar must also agree.

Another shared browser case checks actual tools-host ownership and absence of ScrollView in the opt-in host, wheel/Home/accessible-page commands, offscreen clipping, editor reveal, AX range and reopen bounds on both backends. Existing tools resize/header/status, history row, action and selector clipping/capture cases keep their original semantic assertions through the common viewport interface. Broader actual Cocoa keyboard/editor/IME and presentation-backed scene tests remain included.

No dependency or browser-service policy was added. Preferences/other scroll containers, platform scrollbar/event/AX/window adapters, stable Rust interaction/node ownership and full manual/performance/release acceptance remain open. No controlled CPU/GPU/presentation or memory gain is established.

initial_viewport_probe.note: Both backends initially passed wheel/key/AX/reveal but failed the oracle range assertion after content ceased overflowing. Chromium retains the hidden scrollbar old maximum (280), while the effective content/viewport range is zero on both implementations. The oracle now compares live extents and also checks the bar maximum whenever visible. No production viewport behavior changed for this correction; all four sizes and 80 requests remain. Initial sources/binary identity/failures are retained, not counted as passing current results.

before_native_observer_cleanup.note: A pre-cleanup broad run passed 90 Metal/72 Views. The native Views adapter then dropped its unnecessary Metal refresh observer to preserve the original native paint path; final focused/broad/full results below use the rebuilt corrected source/binary. Only the old sidebar_layout.cc differs and is retained with this snapshot.
